subject: Post-call recap: AcmeHealth Private/VPC discovery — networking & data residency
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmehealth.com>, Meera Shah <mshah@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: AcmeHealth Private/VPC discovery — networking & data residency

Hi Sanjay / Meera,

Thanks again for taking time today — really helpful to walk through AcmeHealth's constraints and goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps below. Let me know if I missed anything.

Call highlights / pain points:
- Primary driver: regulatory data residency and audit requirements (state-level PHI controls + upcoming SOC 2 requirement). You need all inference traffic and logs to remain inside AcmeHealth-controlled VPCs and be auditable.
- Networking constraints: customer-managed egress rules (only TLS to approved endpoints), strict firewall rules, and mandatory proxy for outbound traffic.
- Air-gap option: for critical PHI workloads you may require an air-gapped on-prem deployment. This is a separate product track but we can support with Private (on-prem) package + offline image.
- Latency/cost: current target is <100ms p95 for chat endpoints; heavy throughput on batch scoring for nightly jobs.

What Redwood proposes (summary):
- Private/VPC deployment with customer-managed VPC peering or private link to keep data in-region.
- Optional on-prem air-gapped bundle for sandboxed PHI processing (requires network diagram + maintenance window planning).
- Integration checklist: KMS/HSM for key management, audit log forwarding to your SIEM, and cert pinning for outbound telemetry.

Open questions we agreed to follow up on:
1) Exact list of IP ranges and proxy headers for our egress endpoints so you can validate with security.
2) Whether the nightly batch scoring can run on Dedicated capacity in your cloud vs fully on-prem (affects pricing and footprint).
3) Any procurement timeline / SOW constraints from your legal team.

Attachments included: networking requirements template (acmehealth-networking-requirements.xlsx) and a draft architecture diagram (redwood-private-deploy-arch.png).

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll share the networking template and a short MOP (method-of-provision) for the on-prem bundle by EOD Thursday.
- Dev (cc'd) to follow up with a short checklist of firewall/proxy headers and our IP ranges.
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra/security team next week (Sanjay/Meera: what days work?).

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Meera Shah <mshah@acmehealth.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: AcmeHealth Private/VPC discovery — networking & data residency

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Correct on the drivers; PHI residency is mandatory for the pilot (state-level rules and our SOC 2 roadmap).
- For the initial pilot, we prefer the Private/VPC approach with VPC peering to avoid public egress (we can review PrivateLink if that simplifies approvals).
- Air-gap: we will defer on full air-gapped for pilot but want the option documented and priced.
- IP ranges: I’ll check with our network team and send the approved proxy/IP allowlist. Expect that by Friday.

Questions for Redwood: 
- Can you confirm whether telemetry (health checks/metrics) can be routed to a customer-managed metrics endpoint in our VPC (instead of Redwood-managed telemetry)?
- For KMS: we run AWS KMS with a customer-managed CMK. We need a brief on how Redwood integrates with CMK/HSM for encryption-at-rest and key rotation.

Also looping in Meera for procurement timelines — we’d like a statement of work and ballpark numbers for both Private/VPC and an on-prem air-gap option.

Regards,
Sanjay Rao
Head of Infrastructure | AcmeHealth
Sanjay.Rao@acmehealth.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmehealth.com>, Meera Shah <mshah@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: AcmeHealth Private/VPC discovery — networking & data residency

Dev / Ethan — looping you in to pick up the technical follow-ups. Action items: 

- Dev: please prepare the IP ranges, outbound proxy header list, and an outline of options for PrivateLink vs VPC peering. Put items into the networking template and return to Sanjay by Friday morning.
- Ethan: draft a short note (1–2 pages) on our KMS/HSM integration flow and how key rotation is handled for customer-managed CMKs. Also include any limitations for on-prem air-gapped rotations.
- I'll draft the two SOW/ballpark pricing options (Private/VPC + on-prem air-gapped) and share with Meera for procurement. Target: first draft by Friday EOD.

Sanjay / Meera — is Friday 10am PT for a technical deep-dive reasonable? If yes, Dev will send a calendar invite with agenda (networking checklist, KMS integration, deployment footprint).

Thanks —
Marissa
